key_insight: AdamX is a first-order optimizer that uses cosine similarity to adapt update magnitudes while adding variance rectification for smoother early training.
engineering_relevance: It is designed to be model-agnostic, easy to plug into existing pipelines, and scalable for practical deep learning training.
method: Uses cosine similarity as an adaptive control signal for step sizes.
Adds a variance rectification scheme to stabilize early optimization.
Targets straightforward integration into standard optimizer workflows.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports empirical evaluation across multiple benchmark datasets and architectures, measuring how many epochs are needed to hit predefined performance thresholds under a fixed hyperparameter budget.
watch_item: The abstract does not provide detailed comparisons, so practical gains may depend on tuning, task, and architecture specifics.
paper_title: AdamX: Cosine similarity meets gradient descent
